long.topic: Your map of Brunei shows a country cut in two pieces by a strip of Malaysia (Limbang), and you cross Malaysia twice, with passport stamps, to drive from one half of Brunei to the other. The countdown runs: 7) Brunei split in two, 6) The Gambia, a thin strip about 25-50 km wide that runs along a river and is surrounded by Senegal on every side except the sea, 5) Azerbaijan's Nakhchivan exclave, cut off from Azerbaijan by Armenia, 4) Angola's Cabinda, cut off from Angola by a strip of DR Congo, 3) Oecusse, East Timor's exclave inside Indonesian West Timor, 2) the Dahagram-Angarpota Bangladeshi enclave inside India, and 1) India's strangest border of all, the Tin Bigha Corridor, a small strip of Indian land leased to Bangladesh so its citizens can reach Dahagram, with a gate that opens and closes at set hours. Each stop is shown as a simple animated map with the odd shape highlighted on screen, and the video ends on a loop back to the hook and a one-line tease for the next video.

shorts.topic: Your boat trip on Chilika Lake in Odisha crosses India's largest coastal lagoon, a brackish lake where you can spot Irrawaddy dolphins.
Your cruise through Ha Long Bay in Vietnam passes about 1,600 limestone islands rising from emerald water like green towers.
Your map of Bolivia shows two capitals: Sucre, the constitutional capital, and La Paz, where the government sits.
Your teeth, bones and muscles are shown in a spacewalk-style test of astronaut gear. NASA's ISS spacesuit glove check shows a bare hand protected by layers, with the vacuum visible in tests.

Your digital camera in a smartphone sees through thin black plastic: film a bulb through a thin black plastic bag, and near-infrared light passes through so the bulb shows up on screen (works best on some phones, visible on camera).
